query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying a high entropy alloy surface treatment to a Cu matrix will enhance the adhesion properties of the alloy to the Cu surface.
generation.intervention: Surface treatment with a high entropy alloy
generation.conditions: Standard atmospheric conditions during application and curing
generation.structural_mediator: Interfacial bonding between the high entropy alloy and the Cu matrix
generation.mechanism: Modification of surface properties of the Cu matrix to improve mechanical interlocking and chemical bonding with the high entropy alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased adhesion strength between the high entropy alloy and the Cu matrix, leading to improved wear resistance
generation.baseline: Current adhesion strength of materials to Cu matrix without surface treatment
generation.boundary: Effects observed only in surface protection applications involving Cu matrices and high entropy alloys
generation.uncertainty: The specific high entropy alloy and the exact conditions for optimal adhesion are not known, leading to uncertainty in the predicted outcomes.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct adhesion tests comparing untreated Cu matrix with Cu matrix treated with high entropy alloy surface treatment.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the adhesion strength of the treated Cu matrix is not significantly greater than that of the untreated matrix, the hypothesis is falsified.
